headline: Testing identifiability and assumptions behind transcriptomic inference models
label: Transcriptomic Model Validation Design
summary: Expression-based inferences are being stress-tested for context dependence, component identifiability and cross-state coherence rather than fit alone.
synthesis: The common thread across these preprints is scrutiny of the assumptions underlying transcriptomic inference rather than reliance on model fit alone. A threshold-free, copy-number-adjusted pan-cancer framework applied to PTK2 across 17 TCGA cohorts models context-dependent co-expression by separating conforming from nonconforming programmes rather than discarding them. A Hi-C-based accessibility index, RFA, is evaluated as a 3D-aware GRN filter and is reported to anticorrelate with eQTL through distance-decay while showing no predictive value for ΔRNA. A reanalysis of 252,106 drug-treated glioma cells asks whether response direction is coherent across malignant states rather than collapsed into a single average. What is new is the focus on whether model components can be distinguished and whether their assumptions hold, with the RFA result illustrating that a plausible regulatory-structure proxy may carry no predictive content for expression change.
